title: Target anatomy
view: Parasagittal section of the right upper back at about T5, 3 cm from the midline, under a sagittal probe, as on ultrasound: cranial on the image left, caudal on the right, skin at the top. Composition after NYSORA's plate (concept only).
teachingPoint: The needle passes through trapezius, rhomboid and erector spinae until the tip touches a transverse process; the injectate lifts the erector spinae and spreads cranially and caudally along the processes.
claims: Sagittal probe about 3 cm lateral to the spinous processes (record).
Trapezius, rhomboid major and erector spinae in three layers over the transverse processes at T5 (NYSORA; record: erector spinae over the square transverse processes).
Transverse processes as squared bony blocks, about 4 cm deep and about 26 mm apart (standard anatomy, typical adult depth).
Superior costotransverse ligament between the processes, paravertebral fat and pleura deep to it (standard anatomy).
Needle in-plane from cranial, tip touching the middle transverse process (record steps 3-4).
Teal: spread deep to the erector spinae over the processes, running cranially and caudally (record: spreads deep to the erector spinae).
Labels: Trapezius, Rhomboid major, Erector spinae, Transverse process, Pleura.

geometry.why: transverse process deep to the erector spinae
needle cranial to caudal (cranial on the left)
tip touches the process, not into it
needle stays well above the pleura
spread lies along the deep surface of the erector spinae
spread on the processes, not in bone
